newsitem.title: GERMANY: German investment slumps in 1996 - Bundesbank.
newsitem.headline: German investment slumps in 1996 - Bundesbank.

text.p: German public and private investment in fixed assets and inventories slumped last year to its lowest since 1993 as the weak economy provided little incentive to build capital stocks, the Bundesbank said.

The German central bank said in its monthly report for May total investment in fixed assets and inventories fell to 295.8 billion marks from 325.4 billion marks in 1995 to hit the lowest level since 1993 when investment totalled 257.1 billion marks.
The Bundesbank said investment was hurt in part because much of Germany's economic growth last year came from the export sector and that domestic oriented companies saw scant growth.
High taxes and labour costs also dampened investment, especially among west German companies, the Bundesbank added.
Investment by German companies shrank to 240.7 billion marks from 264.3 billion marks while public sector investment shrank to 55.1 billion marks from 61.1 billion marks.
Savings by private households, meanwhile, climbed to their highest level since 1992 as total savings hit 233.1 billion marks, up from 222.3 billion marks.
